text:
The taste of sugar is a deceptive comfort: it begins with an immediate, sharp sweetness that promises satisfaction, but lingers with a cloying heaviness that coats the throat, masking the underlying bitterness of what it tries to hide.

Liam stood before the canvas, the smell of turpentine sharp in his nose, but the air in the house was thick with the scent of old money and older expectations. His father, Arthur, did not knock; he entered with the weight of a man who believed ownership was a right, not a privilege. He placed a leather-bound ledger on the easel, right next to Liam’s half-finished portrait of a stormy sea.

"The merger is finalized, Liam," Arthur said, his voice devoid of the warmth Liam remembered from childhood. "The gallery is closed. Effective immediately."

Liam’s brush hovered, a drop of crimson paint trembling at the tip. "Closed? You can’t just—"

"I didn't ask," Arthur interrupted, his eyes cold and calculating. "You have until the end of the week to sign the transfer papers. If you don't, I will sell the studio. And you will work the floor at the warehouse like the rest of them."

The conflict wasn't just about art anymore; it was about survival. Liam looked at the ledger, then at his father. The rift wasn't just a misunderstanding; it was a chasm. Arthur saw Liam’s passion as a liability, a childish whim that threatened the empire they had built. Liam saw his father’s duty as a cage, a gilded prison designed to suffocate his soul.

As Arthur turned to leave, he paused. "Don't make me regret this, son. Loyalty is the only currency that matters in this family."

The door clicked shut, leaving Liam alone with the silence and the crushing weight of the choice. The sugar of his childhood dreams had turned to ash in his mouth, and now, he had to decide whether to swallow the bitterness of obedience or spit it out and face the void.
